title: Destiny's Child
wiki_lead:
Destiny's Child was an American girl group formed in Houston, Texas, in 1990. Through the contributions of its principal members—Beyoncé, Kelly Rowland, Michelle Williams, and original members LaTavia Roberson and LeToya Luckett—the group is regarded as one of the most influential girl groups in popular music. Known for their vocal harmonies, stage performances, and themes of female empowerment, Destiny's Child played a central role in the girl group resurgence of the 1990s and the emergence of rap-singing, while helping shape contemporary R&B.
Starting their musical career as Girl's Tyme, the original quartet—Beyoncé, Rowland, Roberson, and Luckett—were signed to Columbia Records in 1996 as Destiny's Child, gaining recognition with the single "No, No, No". They then released their best-selling album, The Writing's on the Wall (1999), which spawned the US Billboard Hot 100 number-one singles "Bills, Bills, Bills" and "Say My Name". Despite critical and commercial success, the group was plagued by internal conflict and legal turmoil, as Roberson and Luckett attempted to split from the group's manager, Mathew Knowles, due to his favoritism of his daughter Beyoncé and Rowland.
In early 2000,  Williams and Farrah Franklin replaced both Roberson and Luckett; Franklin quit after a few months, leaving the group as a trio. The group's third album, Survivor (2001), drew on the internal conflicts and lineup changes, yielding the US number-one singles "Independent Women" and "Bootylicious". After releasing the Christmas album 8 Days of Christmas (2001), Destiny's Child announced a hiatus so that each member could pursue a solo career. They reunited to release their fifth and final album, Destiny Fulfilled (2004), which produced the US top-three singles "Lose My Breath" and "Soldier".
Since the group officially disbanded in 2006, Beyoncé, Rowland, and Williams have reunited several times, including at the 2013 Super Bowl halftime show, the 2018 Coachella festival, and the final show of the Cowboy Carter Tour (2025). Destiny's Child is one of the best-selling girl groups in history, with estimated sales of over 60 million records. Their accolades include three Grammy Awards, eleven Billboard Music Awards, five American Music Awards, two MTV Video Music Awards, and a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. Billboard named Destiny's Child's final lineup one of the greatest musical trios of all time.

History


1990–1997: Early beginnings and Girl's Tyme
In 1990, Beyoncé met LaTavia Roberson while auditioning for an all-girl entertainment group. Based in Houston, Texas, they joined a group that performed rap and dance routines on the city's talent show circuit. Kelly Rowland, who lived in Beyoncé's house at the time, joined them in 1992. Originally named Girl's Tyme, they were eventually reduced to six members, including Támar Davis and sisters Nikki and Nina Taylor. grok_lead: Destiny's Child was an American R&B and pop girl group whose final and most successful lineup consisted of BeyoncÃ© Knowles, Kelly Rowland, and Michelle Williams. Formed in Houston, Texas, in 1997, the group achieved massive commercial success in the late 1990s and early 2000s through a blend of empowering lyrics, harmonious vocals, and infectious hooks, becoming one of the best-selling female acts in music history with over 50 million records sold worldwide. Their discography includes five studio albums, numerous chart-topping singles, and two Grammy Awards, all while navigating lineup changes and setting the stage for the solo stardom of their members. The group's origins trace back to the early 1990s, when BeyoncÃ© Knowles and LaTavia Roberson, both around nine years old, formed an initial act called Girl's Tyme in Houston, later expanding to six members including Kelly Rowland, LeToya Luckett, TÃ¡mar Davis, and sisters Nikki and Nina Taylor. After performing locally and auditioning unsuccessfully for labels, the core quartet of Knowles, Rowland, Roberson, and Luckett signed with Columbia Records in 1996, rebranding as Destiny's Child the following year. Their self-titled debut album arrived in 1998, peaking at number 67 on the Billboard 200 and earning platinum certification, driven by the lead single "No, No, No" which reached number three on the Hot 100. Breakthrough stardom came with their sophomore release, The Writing's on the Wall (1999), which sold over 8 million copies in the U.S. alone and featured the group's first number-one hits: "Bills, Bills, Bills" and "Say My Name." The latter track earned Destiny's Child their first two Grammy Awards in 2001 for Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals and Best R&B Song, highlighting their vocal synergy and songwriting prowess. However, internal tensions led to the departure of Luckett and Roberson in 1999 amid management disputes, briefly introducing Farrah Franklin as a replacement before she left after five months; Michelle Williams then joined in 2000, solidifying the iconic trio. The trio's chemistry propelled their third album, Survivor (2001), to number-one status on the Billboard 200, with quadruple-platinum sales in the U.S. and global hits including "Independent Women Part I" (from the Charlie's Angels soundtrack), "Survivor," and " Bootylicious." This era also saw holiday album 8 Days of Christmas (2001) and remix collection This Is the Remix (2002), maintaining their momentum with tracks like "Jumpin', Jumpin'." Their final studio album, Destiny Fulfilled (2004), debuted at number two on the Billboard 200 and produced top-ten singles " Lose My Breath " and " Soldier," before the group announced their disbandment during a 2005 world tour to pursue individual paths.
